==Problem==
Peter lives near a rectangular field that is filled with blackberry bushes. The field is 10 meters long and 8 meters wide, and Peter can reach any blackberries that are within 1 meter of an edge of the field. The portion of the field he can reach is shaded in the figure below. What fraction of the area of the field can Peter reach?

[[File:2026 amc 8 q6.png | center | 650px]]

<imath>\textbf{(A) } \frac{1}{6}\qquad\textbf{(B) } \frac{1}{4}\qquad\textbf{(C) } \frac{1}{3}\qquad\textbf{(D) } \frac{3}{8}\qquad\textbf{(E) } \frac{2}{5}\qquad</imath>

==Solution==
We can calculate this reachable area to be <imath>\text{Total area} - \text{Unreachable area}</imath>. The total area is <imath>8 \cdot 10 = 80</imath>, and the unreachable area is <imath>(8-2)(10-2) = 6\cdot 8 = 48</imath>. Thus, our answer is <imath>\frac{80-48}{80} = \frac{32}{80} = \boxed{ \textbf{(E) } \frac{2}{5} }</imath>.

~OlympiadMaster

==Solution 2==

Each "region" is one unit from an edge. Thus, let <imath> l </imath> be the length and <imath> w </imath> be the width of the unshaded region. Then, it is obvious that <imath> l = 10 - 2 = 8 </imath> and <imath> w = 8 - 2 = 6 </imath>, and the unshaded regions dimensions are <imath> 8 \times 6 </imath>.

Then, the area of the shaded region is the area of the total region subtracted by the area of the unshaded region, or <imath> 80 - 48 = 32 </imath> <imath>\text{un}^2</imath>. Then, the ratio is simply <imath> 32/80 </imath>, or <imath>\boxed{\frac{2}{5}}</imath>.

~Pinotation

==Solution 3==

By rearranging the diagram, the unreachable (white) region can be moved to the lower-left corner without changing the shaded area. The reachable region then forms an L-shaped figure composed of two rectangles.

One rectangle has dimensions <imath>8\times 2</imath> and the other has dimensions <imath>10\times 2</imath>. These rectangles overlap in a <imath>2\times 2</imath> square, which must be subtracted once.

Thus, the area of the shaded region is
<imath>(8\cdot 2)+(10\cdot 2)-(2\cdot 2)=2(10+8-2)</imath>.

The total area of the field is <imath>10\cdot 8=80</imath>. Dividing, the fraction of the field Peter can reach is
<imath>\dfrac{2(10+8-2)}{80}=\dfrac{10+8-2}{40}=\dfrac{16}{40}=\boxed{\textbf{(E)}\ \dfrac{2}{5}}</imath>.

~jeremyq

==Solution 4==
We can first start off by finding the unreachable area. The problem tells us that the distance between the reachable and unreachable area is <imath> 1 </imath>, and since there are <imath> 2 </imath>, we get the dimensions of the unreachable to be <imath> 8 \cdot 6 </imath>, because <imath> 8 = 10 - 2 </imath>, and <imath> 6 = 8 - 2. </imath>. Therefore, the area of the unreachable is <imath> 48 </imath>. However, the problem asks us to find the fraction of area he can reach, so we need to get area of the entire field and subtract by <imath> 48 </imath>.Since the entire field is <imath> 8 \cdot 10 = 80 </imath>,  we get <imath> 80 - 48 = 32 </imath>. So the area of the part Peter can reach is <imath> 32 </imath>. Finally, to convert this to a fraction of the entire field, we can do <imath> \frac{32}{80} </imath>, so our answer is <imath> \frac{32}{80} = \boxed{ \textbf{(E) } \frac{2}{5} }</imath>.

~Ingeniouspeacock36
